slides.head:
Google now rents AI worlds you can
walk through, by the second.
Genie 4 is out.
slides.body: On November 18 Google put Genie 4 in Project Genie for eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers. A day later it opened to developers in the Gemini API and Google AI Studio.

slides.head: Worlds you can steer.
slides.body: A text prompt, a reference image, or both, becomes a world you move through with the keyboard. New prompts change weather, lighting or events mid-session.

slides.head: Sound is built in.
slides.body: Google says it is the first Genie model with real-time native audio: ambient sound and character dialogue that adapt to the scene.

slides.head: About 10 cents a second.
slides.body: Google's docs list about $0.10 per second of streamed output. Sessions run up to 120 seconds at 720p and 24 fps.

slides.head: A sketchpad, not a set.
slides.body: Two minutes at 720p does not replace a shoot or a game engine. It is a quick way to walk through an idea before you build it.
